9ea80040.stated: No employee threshold; Art. 37(1) is activity-based; 250 is Art. 30(5)
9ea80040.evidence: 'There is no employee threshold'; Art. 37(1) lists public authority, large-scale monitoring, large-scale special-category/criminal data; 'The 250-employee figure appears in Article 30(5), which concerns an exemption from record-keeping duties, not DPO appointment'.
9ea80040.note: German 20-person rule (raised from 10 in 2019) and the dropped early-draft 250 trigger are accurate.

b5bd3969.stated: No employee threshold; Art. 37(1) is activity-based; 250 is Art. 30(5)
b5bd3969.evidence: 'There is no employee-count threshold. The GDPR never makes a DPO mandatory at any number of employees'; Art. 37(1)(a)-(c) quoted; '250 employees | Art. 30(5) GDPR ... It has nothing to do with DPOs'.
b5bd3969.note: Key items right; outside the key it mislabels WP243 as the DPIA guidelines (WP243 is the DPO guideline) and cites 'EDPB Guidelines 8/2022 on data protection officers', which are actually the lead-supervisory-authority guidelines, so the claim that they 'state expressly that no employee-number threshold exists' is unsupported.
